description: HOLE-ACTIVE-BODY, Feature Scope. Two 40x25x10 mm blocks as two bodies: A at x 0..40 and B at x 60..100 (merge=false, the active body). A through Hole (diameter 6 mm) is placed at the centre of B's +X end face (100, 12.5, 5), drilling along -X, with scope_bodies = [A] (SolidWorks' Feature Scope). The one coaxial bore must cut the owner B AND the scoped A along the full 40 mm length of each.
derivation: Each block: 40 x 25 x 10 = 10000 mm^3, less a bore pi * 3^2 * 40 = 360*pi mm^3 along its full x length.
Area per block: 3300 - 2 * 9*pi (two end discs lost) + 2*pi*3*40 = 240*pi (bore wall) = 3300 + 222*pi. Total 6600 + 444*pi = 7994.867138193868 mm^2.

Centroid: the bore runs along each block's own central axis (y = 12.5, z = 5) through its full length, so each block keeps its centroid (20, 12.5, 5) and (80, 12.5, 5); equal volumes give (50, 12.5, 5).
Topology per block: 6 planar faces + 1 bore cylinder = 7 faces; 12 block edges + 2 bore circles + 1 seam = 15 edges. Total 14 faces, 30 edges, 2 shells.
Mesh (linear_deflection 0.1): 1060 vertices / 1040 triangles, equal to the mesh of the independent build123d construction of the same two drilled blocks.
Independently cross-checked against a direct build123d construction (each Box - the same Cylinder) in tests/test_hole_owner_body.py::test_goldens_match_an_independent_build123d_construction.
tolerance_rationale: Pure boolean cuts of one right cylinder from two boxes; GProp integrates the analytic quadric exactly (the hole goldens' 1e-9).
